title: Ekantik dharma: four together
hookLine: a scripture made of questions asked out loud in a village courtyard, and a love for God that needs three companions
carry: ekantik dharma: dharma, self-knowledge, detachment and bhakti together
tomorrow: A letter that begins with no harm

cards: Evening in a village in Gujarat. A courtyard, a raised seat, a crowd on the ground: farmers, merchants, robed sadhus, children at the edges. The teacher on the seat is Swaminarayan, and he invites questions.
Someone asks a hard one. Why does the mind keep running back to the same old cravings, even after years of devotion? He answers.
Someone pushes back. He answers again. And off to one side, a few senior sadhus listen very closely, because they're going to write this down.
Today, a holy book that began as a conversation.

teach.b: The book is the Vachanamrut. Followers hear the title as vachan, words, and amrut, the nectar of immortality: nectar in the form of words.

teach.h: A SCRIPTURE THAT BEGINS AS DIALOGUE
teach.b: They hold it as scripture, his own teaching, gathered from talks in Gadhada and other villages, each headed with the place, the setting, even what he was wearing that evening. First, its shape. It arrives as dialogue.
A devotee asks, Swaminarayan answers, and sometimes he turns it around and asks the room. Then, the questions. How do you know if your devotion is real?
What do you do with anger toward someone in your own community? Why does a person who has heard good teaching still not change? Kitchen-table questions, treated as worth a scripture.

Last, the answer at its heart, which the tradition calls ekantik dharma: a whole-hearted life held up by four things together. Dharma, doing what's right. Knowing the self, the atman, as distinct from the body.
Vairagya, detachment. And bhakti, love for God.

Many teachers in the tradition read the four this way: love for God without right conduct goes hollow; detachment without love goes dry; knowing the self without devotion can turn proud. Picture the legs of a cot.
Take one away and the whole thing tips. So when someone in the courtyard asks why old cravings keep coming back after years of devotion, the answer, read this way, isn't only pray harder.

how: In Swaminarayan mandirs and homes, passages from the Vachanamrut are read aloud and explained at gatherings, and devotees study it together.

o: a hymnbook his poet-sadhus sang at evening prayer
the Vachanamrut, his teaching kept as questions and answers
a biography of his walk across India as a boy

s: the Vachanamrut is a book of hymns
it's a book of conversations: questions asked by devotees and Swaminarayan's answers.
each talk is headed with where it happened and the setting
even what he was wearing that evening is often recorded.
in the Vachanamrut's ekantik dharma, bhakti alone is enough
bhakti stands with dharma, knowing the self and detachment: all four together.

games.q: you pray every day and love God, but you're short with your family and can't let go of your stuff. by the Vachanamrut's ekantik dharma, what's missing?
o: nothing; love for God covers everything.
dharma and detachment, standing beside your bhakti.
stop praying until your manners improve.
games.why: ekantik dharma holds four together: dharma, knowing the self, detachment and bhakti. the love is real; it needs the other three to stand.

practice: Give one breath to each leg of the cot: doing what's right, knowing yourself as more than the body, letting go, and love, for one face or, if you pray, for God.
Then notice, without judging, which leg feels steady today and which one wobbles, and rest on the whole cot for a few breaths.

wordCard.voice: Gujarat's Swaminarayan. Today, the Vachanamrut, his teaching kept as questions and answers, and its heart: ekantik dharma, four things held together. Today's word.

orig.note: vachan, speech, joined to amrut, the nectar of immortality.

carryVoice: Your line: ekantik dharma, dharma, self-knowledge, detachment and bhakti together. In his courtyard, love for God never stood alone. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Vachanamrut (the recorded discourses of Swaminarayan), its form and recurring themes
